title: Mutual Struct Referencing (Bidirectional Association)
pattern: Two structures maintain direct references to each other, creating a cyclic dependency graph at the type level.
why_bad: In Rust, this leads to memory leaks (reference cycles) and forces the use of verbose, run-time mutation wrappers (`Rc<RefCell<T>>`). It also prevents independent testing and reuse.
detection: Struct `A` contains a field referring to struct `B`, and struct `B` contains a field referring to struct `A` (directly or transitively).
counterexample: Inherent cyclic data structures like doubly-linked lists or tree nodes with parent pointers, though these are typically localized inside safe internal abstractions.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Inappropriate Intimacy"); Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 5 ("Circular Dependencies").
